title: On-demand PDF rendering blocks the FastAPI event loop
reasoning: The route is declared async, but the first PDF download performs synchronous PDF generation directly in the request handler with no await, threadpool offload, background job, or cached in-progress state. PDF rendering is CPU and filesystem heavy, so one first-time PDF download can block the event loop and stall unrelated API requests served by the same worker until rendering completes.
reproduction: Enable PDF downloads, create a completed digest without an existing PDF, then issue GET /api/digests/{digest_id}/download?format=pdf while concurrently polling a lightweight endpoint on the same worker. The lightweight request will not be serviced until synchronous PDF rendering returns.
recommendation: Run PDF generation outside the event loop, for example with FastAPI/Starlette run_in_threadpool, or pre-generate PDFs in the worker and have this route only serve completed files. Consider recording an in-progress generation state so duplicate requests do not trigger duplicate work.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The existing download-format tests assert a successful PDF response and file creation, but they do not exercise concurrent requests or verify that the async server remains responsive during first-time PDF generation.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an async test that monkeypatches PdfGenerator.generate to block on a synchronization primitive, starts a PDF download request, then verifies another lightweight API request can complete before the generator is released.
minimumFixScope: Change only the PDF-missing branch in download_digest_by_id to offload or precompute the blocking PdfGenerator.generate call.
